A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BAPO research, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. V5's added theoretical appendix and relocated experimental material can be reliably distinguished from retained content.

before.justification: V4 reports original LLM accuracy experiments on synthetic reasoning problems, hotel-review tasks, and variable tracking, plus reasoning-token measurements in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V5 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix D, including accuracy comparisons and reasoning-token measurements.

M1.justification: V4 sketches a possible additional attention pass. V5 Appendix C introduces score-based token selection, sequential attention layers, full-input attention, and their combinations, including a multi-hop induction-head construction. These substantially extend the computational model while retaining the original BAPO.

E1.justification: The evaluated synthetic problems, SPACE hotel-review tasks, and RULER-inspired variable tracking are retained. Regular languages, extrema retrieval, and induction heads are theoretical additions without new empirical evaluations.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain GPT-4o/mini, Claude 3.5 Sonnet/Haiku, and Gemini 1.5 Pro/Flash, with o3 and Gemini 2.5 Flash retained in the reasoning comparisons. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: V4 Appendix C.1 and v5 Appendix D.1 retain the data-generation procedures, model configurations, sample counts, accuracy metric, and CoT settings, including the 250-word prompt limit. Prompt spelling corrections do not substantively change the protocol.

E4.justification: The CoT comparisons, DISJOINTNESS versus INTDISJOINTNESS representation check, and vocabulary-size analyses are retained. The new robustness material in Appendix C concerns mathematical assumptions and proofs, assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 independent problem instances and 95% t-test confidence intervals, with the same uncertainty displays. No run-count, seed, or statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The empirical plots and findings in Figures 1, 3–5, and 9–13 are unchanged after matching relocated figures; their graph drawing data also match. Table 1's added regular-language bound is a theoretical result, assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V5 adds Theorem 2 on regular-language recognition, Proposition 2 on extrema and positional retrieval, and Theorems 9–10 on multi-hop induction heads and hardness under generalized attention. Appendix B also corrects several return values, argument orders, and indices in existing proofs. These are substantial mathematical additions beyond renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the effective-bandwidth hypothesis, the BAPO-easy/hard distinction and its empirical alignment, and constant-bandwidth CoT universality. The added theory does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6 replaces conjectural model refinements with an interpretation that core hardness persists under richer attention, while induction heads expose a gap between basic BAPOs and LLM capabilities. Section 3.1 adds the qualification that regular-language recognition depends on language state complexity.

D1.justification: API versions and parameters, prompts, data processing, runtime and cost information, and code/data links are retained. Checklist item 13 now points to the repository instead of describing attached supplementary code, but that repository and its reproduction instructions were already disclosed in v4.

R1.justification: V5 adds Nerode's 1958 work for the regular-language result and removes Sipser's textbook citation. It also develops the connection to previously cited induction-head research; the broader positioning against transformer expressivity and communication-complexity research remains intact.

P1.justification: Sections 3.1 and 3.2 are retitled around BAPO-easy and BAPO-hard problems, the new generalizations appendix is inserted, and Experiments moves from Appendix C to D. Local prose, terminology, acknowledgments, and grammar are edited without extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a regular-language row and state-complexity explanation. Existing figures and appendix tables are redistributed, including Figures 3 and 4 appearing together on v5 page 8. Plot designs and axes are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 leaves richer attention models and the persistence of hardness under additional attention passes as conjectural future work. V5 Appendix C supplies constructions and hardness arguments addressing whether the central conclusions depend on restrictive modeling assumptions. Together with the regular-language theorem and corrections to existing proofs, this substantially strengthens the theoretical foundation while preserving the empirical evidence.
